Tidy and Glance Methods for Chemometric Models

Source: R/tidy_models.R
specproc-tidy-models.Rd

tidy() lists the estimates of a chemometric model in a long tibble, and glance() summarizes the model in a one-row tibble, following the conventions of the broom package. Through parsnip, they also apply to the fitted models and workflows of the "rsimpls", "lts", "rsimca" and "mcd" engines.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'specproc_robpca'
tidy(x, matrix = "eigenvalues", ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_robpca'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_rsimpls'
tidy(x, matrix = "coefficients", ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_rsimpls'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_rpcr'
tidy(x, matrix = "coefficients", ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_rpcr'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_lts'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_lts'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_rsimca'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_rsimca'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_robust_da'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_robust_da'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_opls'
tidy(x, matrix = "coefficients", ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_opls'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_som'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_som'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_wavelength_selection'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_wavelength_selection'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_nas'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_nas'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_domain'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_domain'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An object returned by robpca(), rospca(), macropca(), cellpca(), rsimpls(), rpcr(), lts_fit(), rsimca(), robust_da(), opls(), som(), select_wavelengths(), nas() or applicability_domain().

matrix

The table to return (see Details).

...

Not used.

conf.int

A logical: add the confidence interval (FALSE, default).

conf.level

The confidence level of the interval. Default is 0.95.

Value

A tibble.

Details

tidy() returns, choosing the table with matrix when a model has several:

  • robust PCA (robpca(), rospca(), macropca(), cellpca()): "eigenvalues" (default), one row per component PC with its eigenvalue and std.dev; "loadings", the value of each variable (column) on each PC; "scores", the value of each observation (row) on each PC, as tidy() of a prcomp object in broom (whose names of the tables are also accepted, such as "rotation" and "x");

  • rsimpls() and rpcr(): "coefficients" (default), the estimate of each term (the intercept and the variables) for each response, in the units of the responses; "components", the robust r.squared and the rmse of the models with 1 to kmax components (ncomp); "loadings" and "scores", as for robust PCA;

  • lts_fit(): the term, estimate, std.error, statistic and p.value of the reweighted least-squares fit, and, with conf.int = TRUE, its confidence interval (conf.low, conf.high);

  • rsimca() and robust_da(): one row per class, with its prior, the number n of its regular observations and their misclassification rate error, and, for RSIMCA, its number of components ncomp and the cutoffs of the score and orthogonal distances (cutoff.sd, cutoff.od);

  • opls(): "coefficients" (default), the estimate of each term (variable) with its vip and ortho.vip; "components", the explained variances r2x, r2y and q2 of each component, their cumulative values (r2x.cum, ...) and their significance;

  • som(): one row per unit of the map, with its row and col in the grid, its position (x, y), the number n of observations it represents and their mean quantization error qe;

  • select_wavelengths(): one row per variable (term), with its importance, whether it is selected, and, for iPLS, its interval;

  • nas(): the regression vector, the estimate of each term;

  • applicability_domain(): one row per component PC of the PCA, with its std.dev, percent of the variance and cumulative percent (as fractions).

glance() returns the number of observations nobs and of variables nvar, and:

  • robust PCA: the number of components k, h, alpha, the cutoffs cutoff.sd and cutoff.od, the numbers of n.good.leverage, n.orthogonal.outlier and n.bad.leverage observations, the number of flagged.cells (MacroPCA and cellPCA) and the method;

  • rsimpls() and rpcr(): ncomp, kmax, h, alpha, the robust r.squared, the robust scale of the residuals sigma (one response), the numbers of n.good.leverage, n.vertical.outlier and n.bad.leverage observations, the method and, for RPCR, the regression;

  • lts_fit(): the robust r.squared, the robust scale of the residuals sigma, df.residual, alpha and the number of n.outliers (weight 0 in the reweighted fit);

  • rsimca() and robust_da(): the number of n.classes, the overall misclassification rate error, alpha, the number of observations left out (n.outliers; for RSIMCA, those outlying for all classes) and the method;

  • opls(): the numbers of predictive and orthogonal components (ncomp, ncomp.ortho), r2x.cum, r2y.cum, q2.cum, rmsee and, after a permutation test, its p-values p.r2y and p.q2;

  • som(): the number of n.units, the topology, the quantization.error and topographic.error of the map, the number of n.novel observations (beyond the cutoff of the quantization error), the epochs and whether the map is robust;

  • select_wavelengths(): the method, ncomp, the number of selected variables n.selected, robust, the threshold and, for iPLS, the rmsecv of the final model;

  • nas(): the method, ncomp and the figures of merit (sensitivity, selectivity and, with a noise level, analytical.sensitivity, lod and loq);

  • applicability_domain(): the number of components k, the variance explained, the conf.level and the limits t2.limit and q.limit.

See also

specproc-tidy for the fits, calibrations and plasma diagnostics

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

data(forageLIBS)
wl <- as.numeric(names(forageLIBS[-(1:14)]))
spectra <- forageLIBS[-(1:14)][, wl > 380 & wl < 430]
set.seed(1)
fit <- rsimpls(spectra[1:300, ], forageLIBS$Ca[1:300], ncomp = 4)
tidy(fit, matrix = "components")
#> # A tibble: 10 × 3
#>    ncomp r.squared   rmse
#>    <int>     <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1     1     0.211 0.141 
#>  2     2     0.491 0.113 
#>  3     3     0.689 0.0885
#>  4     4     0.761 0.0776
#>  5     5     0.762 0.0775
#>  6     6     0.768 0.0765
#>  7     7     0.767 0.0765
#>  8     8     0.767 0.0766
#>  9     9     0.767 0.0765
#> 10    10     0.775 0.0753
glance(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 12
#>    nobs  nvar ncomp  kmax     h alpha r.squared  sigma n.good.leverage
#>   <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <dbl>     <dbl>  <dbl>           <int>
#> 1   300   594     4    10   225  0.75     0.738 0.0918              39
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: n.vertical.outlier <int>, n.bad.leverage <int>,
#> #   method <chr>
# the regression vector, one row per wavelength
head(tidy(fit))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   response term            estimate
#>   <chr>    <chr>              <dbl>
#> 1 y        (Intercept)  1.61       
#> 2 y        380.011254  -0.000000637
#> 3 y        380.096143  -0.00000117 
#> 4 y        380.202312  -0.000000911
#> 5 y        380.285294  -0.000000907
#> 6 y        380.3682761 -0.00000108 

pca <- robpca(spectra, k = 3)
tidy(pca)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>      PC eigenvalue std.dev
#>   <int>      <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1     1 786105711.  28038.
#> 2     2  54636943.   7392.
#> 3     3  39024510.   6247.
glance(pca)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 12
#>    nobs  nvar     k     h alpha cutoff.sd cutoff.od n.good.leverage
#>   <int> <int> <int> <int> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>           <int>
#> 1   368   594     3   276  0.75      3.06    12301.              39
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: n.orthogonal.outlier <int>, n.bad.leverage <int>,
#> #   flagged.cells <int>, method <chr>
